chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, who said:
'I do not know it except from Zurara, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: He does not become a solemn oather until he enters with her.'

key_terms.مُؤْلِياً: Solemn oather (one who takes an oath of abstention from conjugal relations)
key_terms.يَدْخُلَ بِهَا: He enters with her (consummation of marriage)

ai.seo_question: When does a husband become legally considered a mu'li regarding his wife?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the legal prerequisite for the ruling of *Ila'* (solemn oath of abstention), specifying that the oath only takes effect after the marital bond is physically consummated. This distinction is crucial in Shia jurisprudence for determining the waiting period (*Iddah*) and the specific procedures for divorce or reconciliation, ensuring the status is not applied prematurely to non-consummated marriages.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ibn Azina who said, ‘I have no knowledge of it except from Zurara,
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘He does not happen to be a solemn oather until he sleeps with her’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from ibn ‘Udhaynah who has said that

I do not know this Hadith except from Zurarah who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘One can only be in ’ Ila ’ (swearing) against his wife when he goes to bed with her.’”
